assertions.text: Output column is 'Discount?' (percentage or amount off) rather than 'Price?' — making verification simpler. If 'Price?' is used instead, both 'Base price' and 'Price?' columns must be present so the reader can trace the calculation.

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method has a single, uniform assertion pattern applied to all rows — not different assertions per scenario. Validation checks one thing (e.g. error message or acceptance status); pricing checks one thing (e.g. discount or price). No if/switch in assertion logic.

assertions.text: Scenario names and @Description text do not restate values the table already shows. The assertion FAILS if either: (1) a scenario name contains a literal value that also appears in an input cell of the same row; or (2) @Description states a fixed value for an input that is already a column in that table.
assertions.evidence: Scenario names like 'Early-bird discount applies' and 'Group discount applies' are descriptive labels, not literal restatements of cell values. @Description fixes base price and cutoff (not columns) rather than restating column values.

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable. The assertion FAILS if: (1) expectation column holds the same value in every row; (2) every expectation is a verbatim copy of an input cell; or (3) a fixed-return implementation would satisfy every row.
assertions.evidence: validatesNameAndEmail: Accepted? varies (true/false across rows). calculatesPriceAndDiscount: Discount? and Price? vary (20.00/0.00, 80.00/100.00/85.00) across different inputs; no fixed-return impl would pass.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body. The assertion FAILS if: (1) a value needed to predict expectation appears only in method body/field, not in column/title/@Description; (2) the operation cannot be named from headers/cells; or (3) a helper criterion is not stated in table/title/description.
assertions.evidence: @Description explicitly states cutoff date (2025-03-01), base price (£100), group threshold (5+), discount rates (20%, 15%), and no-stacking rule. @TypeConverter is transparent setup, not a hidden criterion. All values needed to predict discount and price are visible.
